title: arXiv AI notable papers — 30 September 2026 batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; ordering is inferred from reported evaluation, cross-list breadth, venue/code signals, and relevance, not popularity. Papers are very recent; citations and independent-attention evidence are sparse. Semantic Scholar citation verification was unavailable at snapshot time.

sections.title: Thinking Before Thinking: Scaling Agentic Inference Through Meta-Reasoning
sections.abstract: Introduces an inference-time controller that explicitly manages workers, memory, next-step choices, and compute budgets for long-running agent tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose agentic meta-reasoning, separating a controller’s structured planning and progress assessment from worker task execution; their reported gains are strongest on longer runs.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says controller overhead can hurt at small compute budgets; the reported comparisons cover four benchmarks and three frontier models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Full text reports higher point estimates in all 12 matched comparisons and average gains of 3.6–4.2 points over direct control across four reasoning/programming benchmarks and three frontier models.

sections.title: STEPQuant: When and Where Errors Matter in Delta-Rule Recurrent State Quantization
sections.abstract: Presents spatial-temporal quantization for recurrent states in linear-attention models, with precision allocation based on error persistence and output impact.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine lifetime-aware bit allocation with key-row/value-column scaling; they report near-FP32-state accuracy at a nominal 6-bit budget and better performance than uniform INT8 at 4 bits on the tested models.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is reported on two hybrid models and 13 short-/long-generation tasks; results do not establish transfer to other architectures or serving workloads.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed across three core AI categories; reports experiments on two models, SGLang integration, over 5× recurrent-state compression and up to 68.7% lower total serving memory, and links code.

sections.title: Learning Meta-Skills for Agent Harness Design in Test-Time AI4AI
sections.abstract: Studies how a fixed-weight Builder can learn reusable support-design principles from a Target’s development-task feedback and use them to construct harnesses for unseen tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce meta-skills—reusable rules for when and how a Builder should provide tools, memory, or workflow support—and evaluate a frozen skill bank on held-out tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evaluation is on two benchmarks with fixed Builder and Target model weights; the target-execution budget excludes the Builder’s harness-construction compute.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in three core AI categories; on Harness-Bench and NewtonBench the authors report an 8.95-point macro-average gain over no-skill construction and 12.02 points over direct delivery of the same skill bank.

sections.title: Counterfactual Video Generation Enables Scalable Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
sections.abstract: Uses generated counterfactual human–object videos and a real-to-sim pipeline to train a humanoid manipulation policy that the authors demonstrate on a real robot without real-world fine-tuning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ PRISM pipeline expands a small set of real demonstrations into synthetic interaction videos, reconstructs physically plausible trajectories, and trains a policy for carrying and dropping objects.
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration covers a handful of object classes and uses onboard depth observations; the abstract does not establish transfer beyond the tested tasks and configurations.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record lists publication at CoRL 2026; it spans robotics, vision, and graphics, and the abstract reports a real-robot demonstration across novel object instances and configurations.

sections.title: Imagine3D-LLM: Teaching MLLMs to Imagine 3D Scenes Before Answering
sections.abstract: Trains a multimodal model to construct a compact 3D Gaussian-splat representation from multiple views and condition its answers on that representation.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors supervise summary tokens with photometric reconstruction and report that this also strengthens cross-frame correspondence in the model’s image features.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated evidence concerns multi-view spatial reasoning and 3D-understanding benchmarks; the abstract gives no evidence for broader multimodal tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record lists NeurIPS 2026; the paper is cross-listed in vision and language, and its abstract reports consistent gains across multiple spatial-reasoning and 3D-understanding benchmarks.

sections.title: Breaking the Uniformity Trap: Scaling Video Diffusion Model via SplitMoE
sections.abstract: Proposes a video-diffusion mixture-of-experts design that separates semantic experts from generic experts and uses prototype-guided routing.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that uniform expert balancing fragments coherent video tokens, and propose separate semantic/generic expert pools with prototype-guided routing and pull-push regularization.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract’s evidence is limited to standard video-generation benchmarks and comparisons at an equivalent activated-parameter budget.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record identifies it as a NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight; the paper is cross-listed in vision and AI, and reports gains over load-balanced MoE baselines on standard video-generation benchmarks at an equivalent activated-parameter budget.

sections.title: It's Not What the Image Shows: Irrelevant Context Destabilises VLM Judges Without Informing Them
sections.abstract: Introduces a 200-sentence stress test and finds that adding either aligned or misleading images changes VLM judge labels, while the two image types have similar effects and do not improve human agreement.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose MIST and report that image presence changes many labels, but the image’s depicted sense explains only a minority of those differences.
sections.unique_caveat: The test uses 200 English sentences and 13 judges; its findings do not alone establish the same effect across other languages, tasks, or model families.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The arXiv record lists acceptance at the Trust-AI-Eval workshop at NeurIPS 2026; cross-listed in language, AI, and vision; the abstract reports results across 13 VLM judges.

sections.title: LongHarness Bench: Stress-Testing Language Model Harnesses for Long-Context Reasoning
sections.abstract: Presents a benchmark for comparing long-context harnesses on adaptive retrieval and reasoning, measuring both accuracy and efficiency.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors construct tasks requiring strategic search through semantically relevant long contexts and argue for measuring harness efficiency alongside answer accuracy.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the paper’s four suites, four harnesses, and tested model set; it does not establish a universal harness ordering.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper introduces four evaluation suites and compares four state-of-the-art harnesses; its reported best macro-average accuracy is 68%, while the same model’s efficiency varies substantially by harness.
